images.caption: Figure 1:The landscape of memory mechanisms in autoregressive video generation. The upper tree positions representative methods along two core dimensions: representational carriers (Forms§3) and preservation goals (Functions§). The bottom panels outline the operational lifecycle (Operations§) and training paradigms (Learning§).

Figure 2:Overview of autoregressive video generation and memory-conditioned generation. (Left) AR video generation encompasses discrete token autoregression and continuous frame-/chunk-wise generation, which differ in the inner generation process but share the same causal outer rollout over visual units. (Right) Under bounded local context, a persistent memory state retains information from distant history and conditions the step-wise generator together with the current context and external conditions, enabling an approximation to full-history generation.

Figure 3:Overview of memory carriers in autoregressive video generation. Historical context can persist asvisual memory,implicit state memory,explicit state memory, oradaptive parametric memory, each comprising distinct carrier forms. These memory types can be combined to condition the causal backbone for subsequent generation.

Table 2:Carrier-centric taxonomy of selected memory mechanisms
(Part I: Visual and Implicit State Memory).Carrierdenotes the persistent object read by a later generation step.SGdenotes resident-storage growth with rollout length (Fixed, Bounded, Linear, or scene-scaled);USdenotes unit structure (Itemized, Distributed, Structured, Entity, or Hybrid);Keygives the signal or index used to access a retained historical unit;Noneindicates no separately addressable historical unit;Int.,Edit., andMCdenote interpretability, direct editability of instance-specific memory without retraining, and model coupling, respectively.,, anddenote low, medium, and high levels, respectively.
